newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda says Zaire's problems are self-inflicted.
newsitem.headline: Uganda says Zaire's problems are self-inflicted.

text.p: Uganda's foreign minister said in an interview published on Wednesday that the uprising by rebels in eastern Zaire was self-inflicted and the international community could not undertake to quash it.

Eriya Kategaya told the government-owned daily New Vision newspaper that the region's problems of instability meant Uganda could not "properly concentrate" on issues of regional cooperation and development.

"What is happening in Zaire...was expected. It was on the agenda, I may say, because when you have a country depending on one person, without established structures, problems start coming up," said Kategaya.
Zaire has been led for 31 years by President Mobutu Sese Seko, who has been convalescing in Europe from cancer treatment for several months.

Zaire accuses Uganda, an outspoken critic of Mobutu and close to Tutsi-led Rwanda, of supporting the Tutsi Banyamulenge rebels who have seized towns in eastern Zaire in a month-old rebellion after Zaire threatened to expel them all.

"The question of the Banyamulenge, I do not see why the Zairean government waited all this time to solve it. Why then did the government say: 'You people pack up and go'? Go where? This is a self-inflicted injury really."
U.N. agencies say that at least 500,000 refugees are "lost" in the hills in eastern Zaire since the Banyamulenge launched the fighting and were rewarded with a string of victories.
